Elżbieta Bogusława November 15, 1985
Dear Ones,
I arrived safely in Paris without any major hitches. In London, I wasn't able to meet up with my cousin—well, as they say, c'est la vie. In Paris, a French customs officer eyed my passport suspiciously but eventually decided to let me through. I suppose the French aren't very fond of communist passports. My passport became the subject of speculation among the American group I was flying with to Paris; I held up the passport control line for about five minutes. After I cleared passport control, people from the American group approached me and asked who I was and what the problem had been. Those are such stereotypical questions. In the end, it all ended with a smile. Alina and Claude were waiting for me. And what comes next? Well, on November 21st, I’m flying to Poland. Once again, I would like to thank you both—my dear uncle and aunt—with my deepest gratitude for looking after me. You cared for me as if I were your own child, and I thank you so very much for that. I will always remember it. I would also really like to take this opportunity to once again dispel Auntie’s doubts regarding her cooking. Dearest Auntie, I truly enjoy your cooking—what you make, and how you make it. Just ask Tosia if I ever complained!
[Second page]
I am currently in the phase of comparing America and France, and I’ve come to the conclusion that—simply put—there’s no place like the USA. I hope you will forgive me for the critical remarks I made during the first few days of my stay with you; I always strive to be objective, and now I can see the vast chasm that separates European countries from the USA. And that is the absolute truth. Once again, thank you both most warmly. Warm regards to you all, my dears.
Bogdan

Declarant/father: Ostap Zając, age 46, a peasant living in Wiski
Witnesses: Tomasz Sławatycki, age 36, and Ludwik Szaniawski, age 40, both peasants living in Wiski
Newborn girl: He "presented to Us an infant of female sex stating that it was born in the village of Wiski on this day at 2 o'clock in the night to his lawful wife Agnieszka née Onyszczuk, 40 years old. At the Holy baptism administered on this day by the clergyman Julian Kriński, this child was given the name Kazimiera, and her godparents were Kazimierz Zębrzycki and Zofia Plewak."
Act signed only by registrar > priest Julian Kriński, the others were illiterate.
